feedback.problem: Given that ${\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-5$ and ${\int }_{4}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x=8$ then what is ${\int }_{0}^{7}(7+3f(x))\,\text{d}x?$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{4}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in the known information into the above gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-5)+8={\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 3={\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute the desired integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{7}(7+3f(x))\,\text{d}x & =7{\int }_{0}^{7}\,\text{d}x+3{\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =7\cdot x{|}_{0}^{7}+3(3) \\  & =7(7-0)+9 \\  & =58.\end{aligned}
$$
